pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B9.3.1)
- B9.3.1.2 — Construct inscribed and circumscribed triangles and parallelograms with given dimensions.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- construct the incentre and the inscribed circle (incircle) of a triangle
- construct the circumcentre and the circumscribed circle (circumcircle) of a triangle
- construct squares, rectangles, rhombuses and parallelograms under given conditions
- construct compound plane shapes

lessons.title: Inscribed and circumscribed circles

pages.title: Inscribed and circumscribed circles
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Draw inscribed and circumscribed circles for triangles under given conditions.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.1.2.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Incentre and incircle** — The three **angle bisectors** of a triangle meet at one point, the **incentre** I. I is the same distance from all three **sides**, so a circle with centre I touches all three sides — the **inscribed circle (incircle)**.
## ✏️ Example 9.1
Construct triangle ABC with AB = 8 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 6 cm. Locate the incentre and draw the inscribed circle. Measure the shortest distance from the incentre to each side. What do you observe?
**Solution**
[[fig:m9-f20]]
Figure 9.1: The incircle touches all three sides
1. Construct the triangle from its three sides.
2. Bisect ∠BAC and ∠BCA (two bisectors are enough). They meet at the incentre L (I).
3. From I drop a perpendicular to any side, meeting it at N. IN is the radius.
4. With centre I and radius IN, draw the circle.
Observation: the perpendicular distances from I to AB, BC and AC are all equal (about **1.9 cm**). Every point on an angle bisector is equidistant from the two arms, so the meeting point of the bisectors is equidistant from all three sides.
> 🔑 **Key idea: Circumcentre and circumcircle** — The three **perpendicular bisectors** of the sides of a triangle meet at one point, the **circumcentre** O (or S). O is the same distance from all three **vertices**, so a circle with centre O passes through A, B and C — the **circumscribed circle (circumcircle)**.

pages.title: Example 9.2
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 9.2
Construct triangle ABC with AB = 7 cm, ∠BAC = 60° and AC = 5 cm. Locate the circumcentre and draw the circumscribed circle. Measure the distance from the circumcentre to A, B and C.
**Solution**
[[fig:m9-f21]]
Figure 9.2: The circumcircle passes through all three vertices
1. Draw AB = 7 cm, construct 60° at A and mark C with AC = 5 cm. Join BC.
2. Construct the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC (a third, of BC, will pass through the same point).
3. They meet at the circumcentre O.
4. With centre O and radius OA, draw the circle. It passes through B and C.
Observation: OA = OB = OC ≈ **3.6 cm** — every point on the perpendicular bisector of a side is equidistant from its two ends.
> ✨ **Did you know?** For an **acute**-angled triangle the circumcentre lies inside the triangle; for a **right**-angled triangle it is the midpoint of the hypotenuse; for an **obtuse**-angled triangle it lies outside. The incentre is always inside.

pages.title: Exercise 9.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 9.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Construct triangle PQR with PQ = 9 cm, QR = 7.5 cm and PR = 6 cm. Construct its incircle and measure its radius.
2. Construct triangle XYZ with XY = 8 cm, ∠X = 45° and ∠Y = 60°. Construct its circumcircle and measure its radius.
3. Construct a right-angled triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Construct its circumcircle. Where is the centre?

questions.q: Construct triangle PQR with PQ = 9 cm, QR = 7.5 cm and PR = 6 cm. Construct its incircle and measure its radius.
Construct triangle XYZ with XY = 8 cm, ∠X = 45° and ∠Y = 60°. Construct its circumcircle and measure its radius.

parts.a: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse; radius 5 cm

pages.title: Constructing parallelograms
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Construct parallelograms (square, rectangle, rhombus) under given conditions.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.1.2.2
| **Shape** | **Sides** | **Angles** | **Diagonals** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Square | all equal | all 90° | equal, bisect each other at 90° |
| Rectangle | opposite sides equal | all 90° | equal, bisect each other |
| Rhombus | all equal | opposite angles equal | bisect each other at 90° |
| Parallelogram | opposite sides equal and parallel | opposite angles equal | bisect each other |
## ✏️ Example 9.3
Construct a square ABCD with AB = 6.5 cm. Measure its diagonal.
**Solution**
1. Draw AB = 6.5 cm. Construct perpendiculars at A and at B.
2. Mark D and C on them so that AD = BC = 6.5 cm (arcs from A and B).
3. Join DC. Check that DC = 6.5 cm.
[[fig:m9-f22]]
Figure 9.3: Square ABCD with side 6.5 cm
Diagonal AC ≈ **9.2 cm** (by Pythagoras: √(6.5² + 6.5²) = 9.19 cm).
## ✏️ Example 9.4
Construct a square with diagonal 8 cm.
**Solution**
The diagonals of a square are equal and bisect each other at 90°.
1. Draw AC = 8 cm and construct its perpendicular bisector, meeting AC at M.
2. Mark B and D on the bisector with MB = MD = 4 cm.
3. Join A, B, C, D. Each side is about 5.7 cm.
## ✏️ Example 9.5
Construct a rectangle PQRS with PQ = 7 cm and diagonal PR = 9 cm.
**Solution**
1. Draw PQ = 7 cm and construct a perpendicular at Q.
2. With centre P and radius 9 cm, cut the perpendicular at R.
3. Complete the rectangle: with centre R radius 7 cm and centre P radius QR, draw arcs meeting at S. Join RS and PS.
QR = √(81 − 49) = √32 ≈ **5.7 cm**.

pages.title: Example 9.6
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 9.6
Construct a parallelogram ABCD with AB = 7 cm, AD = 4.5 cm and ∠DAB = 60°. Construct a rhombus with side 5 cm and one angle of 120°.
**Solution**
Parallelogram: draw AB = 7 cm; construct 60° at A; mark D with AD = 4.5 cm; with centre D radius 7 cm and centre B radius 4.5 cm draw arcs meeting at C; join DC and BC.
[[fig:m9-f23]]
Figure 9.4: Parallelogram with AB = 7 cm, AD = 4.5 cm, ∠A = 60°
Rhombus: the same method with all sides 5 cm and an angle of 120° at the first vertex (the adjacent angles are 60°).
## ✏️ Example 9.7
Construct a compound shape: a square of side 4 cm with an equilateral triangle on its top side, forming a "house" shape. Find the perimeter of the compound shape.
**Solution**
Construct the square with perpendiculars. On the top side, draw arcs of radius 4 cm from both ends to locate the apex, and join. The perimeter consists of 3 sides of the square and 2 sides of the triangle: **5 × 4 = 20 cm**.

pages.title: Exercise 9.2
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 9.2** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Construct a square of side 5.5 cm and measure its diagonal.
2. Construct a rectangle with sides 8 cm and 5 cm. Measure its diagonals.
3. Construct a rhombus with diagonals 8 cm and 6 cm. Measure a side.
4. Construct a parallelogram PQRS with PQ = 6 cm, QR = 4 cm and ∠PQR = 135°. Measure the diagonal PR.
5. Construct a regular hexagon of side 3 cm on top of a rectangle 6 cm by 3 cm (sharing a 3 cm side). Find the perimeter of the compound shape.

pages.title: Chapter 9 summary
pages.body:
- Incentre: meeting point of angle bisectors; incircle touches the sides.
- Circumcentre: meeting point of perpendicular bisectors; circumcircle passes through the vertices.
- Use the properties of sides, angles and diagonals to construct quadrilaterals.
